nodeData.topic: Session 07 · Never Insult Anyone
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. A cultured devotee never insults anyone: Maharaj shows through Suruchi and Dhruva that an offence takes effect in proportion to the purity of the one offended, even if he is only a child at the time. Instead of hunting for pure devotees we should become one, forgive like Haridasa Thakura, look inward when life feels blocked, and preach only where it helps rather than provoking more offences. Questions cover discernment versus fault-finding, sharing one's rounds, correcting seniors, the mind's games and planning tomorrow's japa. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj opens the day's 'surgery': a devotee never insults anyone. Even demons about to fight in the epics challenge one another in ornamented, poetic language. — “a cultural person will not insult”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:44 (auto-transcript): “One of the ways is that we should never insult anyone. a devotee should never insult anyone a cultural person will not a cultural person will not insult in fact even when you see demons are going to fight when they are challenging each other it's so poetic so poetic demons…”

Angada, though furious, spoke to Ravana in measured words and dared him to fight. Jatayu attacked Ravana to rescue Sita; struck hard, Ravana broke the rules of fair combat and cut off his wing with a sword.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:33 (auto-transcript): “When the Angadam met Ravana, he was so angry. Even with that anger, even with that anger, he was speaking to Ravana. You were destined to leave the body by taking Lord Machendra's consult. This is a person who is ready to die.”

Because Jatayu risked his life for the Lord, Rama personally performed his funeral rites and called the holy rivers together to honour him, at a place near Nasik that pilgrims still visit. So we should never insult anyone, but glorify.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:22 (auto-transcript): “Lord Machanda personally did the funeral rites for Jatayu. When you go to Nasik, you can visit a place called Sanket. Sanket, yes. Ramachandran called all the holy rivers to come to Jatayu, to honor him. For drinking water, he could just call only one river, Ganga, whatever.…”

Suruchi insulted Dhruva when he was only a child prince. The offence took effect after he reached perfection: maddened by her son's death, she lost her life.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:15 (auto-transcript): “Serochi's fatal offense. having insulted Dhruva Maharaj Suruchi became maddened upon the death of her son and thus ended her life that is a penalty for insulting somebody and if the person happens to be a pure devotee death penalty and in this case this time Dhruva Maharaj…”

children.topic: We don't know who is who
children.note:
Can we be sure none of the people around us will be a pure devotee tomorrow? Ask those who know each devotee's position and respect accordingly; otherwise treat everyone as well as we can. — “since we don't know who is who, we should treat everyone nicely.”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:25 (auto-transcript): “We have mentioned the other day that since we don't know who is who, we should treat everyone nicely. or we should ask from those who knows what are the positions of different devotees and from their advice follow them in giving them due respect according to their position…”

children.topic: Pierced by the arrow of insult
children.note:
Suruchi told the boy he must die and be born from her womb to sit on his father's lap. Dhruva was pierced by those words; Maharaj recalls Krishna saying in the Eleventh Canto that the arrow of harsh words wounds more than any other.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:02 (auto-transcript): “and surety is sorting through you cannot sit on your father's land. I am saying that you want to climb when your father gets down. Don't sit there. You're not qualified to sit there. If you want to sit there, your qualification is that you should die and take birth in my…”

children.topic: Offence weighs by the devotee's purity
children.note:
The gravity of an offence matches the purity of the one offended. Honour a fully pure devotee and the mercy is complete; offend him and the result is just as complete. — “If you make offense, you also get 100% results.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:25 (auto-transcript): “Okay. the dynamics of the seriousness of offenses is proportionate to the purity and advancement to the devotee who are offended the offense will be greater due to the purity and the devotion of the offended by someone if the devotee is 100% pure the result is 100% pure 100%…”

We speak lofty philosophy and say 'respectful obeisances', yet our faith in one another is small and our doubt large. Maharaj says we are more impersonal toward each other than those we call Mayavadis. — “Our faith is too small.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:16 (auto-transcript): “Yes, such an exalted organization like us. Our experience is that the organization that has less faith is our moment. Our faith is too small. We talk of cultural respect, respect, respect, respectful obeisances. We use this word respectful obeisances. But the amount of the…”

'I have seen so many falldowns; I don't know who is pure.' Would Haridasa Thakura speak like that? No scripture forbids you from being the pure devotee everyone is looking for. — “We should use our time to become a pure devotee.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:04 (auto-transcript): “There's no angel. Why are you not angel? What is the problem? you from me? What's the problem for you being an angel? Is there any scripture that forbids you? There may be written any scripture that this problem should never be a pure devotee or an angel or this matter. It…”

Sometimes the offence is one-sided: the offended devotee is not offensive at all and feels sorry for the offender, knowing what he will suffer. The devotee may forgive, but Krishna may not.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:18 (auto-transcript): “Offenceless Vaisnavas. Sometimes the offense is one-sided. Someone may be very advanced or not so advanced, but not offensive to others. If we offend that devotee, the offense takes place only for the offending party. As a matter of fact, offence-less wise tamas feel sorry…”

children.topic: 'I don't care if it's an offence'
children.note:
Maharaj recalls a devotee who, warned to be careful, said he didn't care and was ready for the results — yet when the reaction came, he blamed everyone else.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:47 (auto-transcript): “but I remember when the devotee was telling Prabhu Prabhu please be careful I said I don't care if I'm making an offence to you. And then what? I don't care. A devotee is saying like that. A devotee. I don't care. The other devotee were trying to, Prabhu, please be careful.…”

'I was falsely accused and you didn't defend me.' If not this time, perhaps in a past life. We say Krishna knows everything; complaining forgets it, as if I were perfect and only others could offend. — “It doesn't mean I have not done it in my past life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:54 (auto-transcript): “And when I was accused unnecessarily, understand? When I was accused unnecessarily, you did not defend me. Right? I was unnecessarily accused. I didn't do anything. A lie was levied on me, but you did not defend me. See, if I have not done the offense this time, It doesn't…”

Beaten in twenty-two marketplaces and still alive, Haridasa Thakura entered trance so that his beaters would not be punished. The Nawab and the Kazi later begged his forgiveness and he gave it.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:13 (auto-transcript): “I don't think Haridah Sekhara was speaking like this. When Haridah Sekhara was beaten after 22 and he was not dying, the people were beating him and complaining, because you are not dying, you're the king who's going to kill us. And I said, oh, is that so? They're okay. I…”

Haridasa felt it was the reaction for not checking those who blasphemed the Lord. Prahlada likewise asked that any blessing go to his sinful father. Whatever happens, a devotee holds on. — “Whatever happened to a devotee, we should not give up Krishna consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:38 (auto-transcript): “what happened. Haridah Sankura noticed that he was so guilty. Nobody was so sorry for what happened to me because when they were blaspheming the Lord, I didn't do anything to check them. So this is the reaction for my nonsense. This is the mentality, this is the mood Haridah…”

children.topic: Do I look outward or inward?
children.note:
Reflection: Haridasa forgave, yet Krishna punished. Is Krishna's justice working in my life through dryness and conflict, and do I call it bad luck instead of correction?

🎙 Maharaj at 42:50 (auto-transcript): “Going into our true reflections. For example, everything is perfectly arranged. When Harada Shephira was building in 22 marketplaces, he forgave all who had offended him, but Krishna punished those who deserved to suffer. Questions for reflection. Is Krishna's justice…”

Most of us look outside — this person, godbrothers, the guru prefers others to me. A sincere, advancing devotee sees no one at fault but himself. — “very dangerous mentality”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:26 (auto-transcript): “When something happens, we don't go inside ourselves to check what I must have done. We only look outside to see who is causing this situation for me. this is what most of us do ah, yes this person, that person ah, guru brothers, sisters krishnas yes, I remember yes, I I have…”

After a few minutes of reflection, devotees share realisations and questions.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:34 (auto-transcript): “so you might share your reflections you may raise your hands so whoever would like to share their reflections so yes we have Shweta Mataji Shweta Mataji would you like to unmute yourself the first questions can you see Krishna means conflict can you see Krishna conflict in…”

children.topic: Q1 · Was my guru correcting me?
children.note:
A devotee wondered why her guru seemed not to listen, then saw it as correction. Maharaj: one who accepts that what happens is the result of his own deeds does not complain but thanks Krishna and the guru — the mood of SB 10.14.8 — and that brings deep inner cleansing.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:47 (auto-transcript): “so yes we have Shweta Mataji Shweta Mataji would you like to unmute yourself the first questions can you see Krishna means conflict can you see Krishna conflict in every sorry I am not well present so can you see Krishna conflict or all those things in our life yes I can…”

How not to confuse discernment with offence when the mind keeps commenting on others' faults? Maharaj: only a mind matured by strong practice responds positively, as a grown child sees the same things differently. — “It's due to maturity.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:49 (auto-transcript): “So these years, after watching your class, I've taken my votes for Katka. Don't make offense and devotes don't insult devotes so on this weekend the kartka i starting see how easily our mind in one conversation or the regular situation in our life is you're starting making a…”

children.topic: Q3 · Should I tell my rounds?
children.note:
Honesty leads a devotee to share things like his number of rounds, and trouble follows. Maharaj: share only with intimate friends, to encourage them; otherwise envy comes from all sides and chanting suffers.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:10 (auto-transcript): “I have a realization and then a question as well so the realization is just recently a couple of days ago I was doing my rounds And it was taking me usually the longer time to chant my rounds, the 16 rounds. And plus, I was also kind of, you know, frequently sleeping while…”

Announcing one's vows to a crowd breeds resentment; between husband and wife it can inspire. Yasoda proposed a vow and Nanda Maharaja joined at once, with no envy — and Krishna came. — “They will hate you, seriously.”

🎙 Maharaj at 62:12 (auto-transcript): “sorry if I may ask one more how do we judge the wrong people Gurudev? I mean, who's wrong? If you know people around you, don't come to the public and say, my dear devotees, since the security have been chanting for children. You see? How many of you are chanting? This is…”

A temple manager asks what to do when arguments flare. Maharaj: go into reflection and pray sincerely to the Supersoul for guidance instead of arguing to prove a point; why worry when you can pray? — “to communicate with the super soul”

🎙 Maharaj at 66:44 (auto-transcript): “Thank you very much. Gurudev, as you told, a culture person does not insult anyone, but actually I am residing in temple, so in temple management we have to deal with so many employees and sometimes devotees so sometimes what happen heated argument and misunderstanding arise…”

children.topic: Polite even at the petrol pump
children.note:
We have a duty to be kind to everyone, even while driving or buying fuel; one who offends us will suffer. If an argument starts, it is best to step away.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:09 (auto-transcript): “level so we can continue with the slides yes yes next one the devotees careful approach we have a duty to be polite and kind to everyone even while drinking even while driving your car or pumping gasoline if someone is offensive to you then they will suffer for that If you…”

Keeping distance is not hatred; it stops us both from becoming more implicated. — “It is love for the person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 71:15 (auto-transcript): “We already discussed it. Keep distance. Keep distance. It is not hatred. It is love for the person. Keep distance. So we don't get implicated and also cause the other person or persons to get more implicated. The Brahma told Osiva, I didn't afford to come to him. The Brahma…”

children.topic: Forgive so they can be rectified
children.note:
Brahma asked Shiva to forgive Daksha so that the sacrifice could be completed. If the offended devotee stays angry, the offender has no chance to be rectified.

🎙 Maharaj at 71:45 (auto-transcript): “The Brahma told Osiva, I didn't afford to come to him. The Brahma told Osiva, when one offends a devotee, there is already heavy consequences waiting for the peace. so that's it that's the reason why a devotee was forgiven so if a devotee becomes angry that means there's no…”

Being right is not enough if it only makes people bitter or provokes them to blaspheme the Society. Non-devotees see insult as normal, and even devotees rarely feel they did wrong, so don't push them into further offences.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:33 (auto-transcript): “We can be right but our right is not benefiting anyone. We may have simply caused that person to become angry or bitter or managed to inspire them to blaspheme us, the society of Krishna. So better to help everyone by the way we behave. We should help everybody the way we…”

If someone grows more disturbed as we share Krishna consciousness, we should stop and tactfully withdraw, so as not to provoke offences.

🎙 Maharaj at 75:23 (auto-transcript): “Yes. We're not to preach protecting others from offense. When someone who we approach for the purpose of sharing Christian concepts becomes more and more disturbed, then we should not preach to them. Because preaching to such a person will make their situation worse. They…”

We only learn whether someone is open by approaching; their response tells us whether to continue. — “Otherwise, there's no need to enter into debate.”

🎙 Maharaj at 76:48 (auto-transcript): “As a text, we have to use to preach. If you want to preach successfully, then we have to know this text. You cannot know if somebody is interested or not interested, or a person is faithless or faithful, until they approach the person. Their responsibility will show us who…”

children.topic: The proud debater and Jiva Gosvami
children.note:
A scholar came to Rupa and Sanatana for debate; they simply signed a letter of defeat. He then went proudly to Jiva Gosvami, who defeated him completely; he fell at his feet, realised the elders' silence had been mercy, and was later initiated.

🎙 Maharaj at 77:38 (auto-transcript): “This is what we see with our Acharyas. Rupa Sanatana Goswami. Rupa Narayan came from. oh just debate you just to debate please we don't have time why do you say debate debate what with the person who you're not going to understand anything so it's why he was very disappointed…”

Philosophy can entertain the intellect but not penetrate the heart. A preacher needs a heart that cannot bear others' suffering. — “And to develop compassion, we must be free from selfishness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 81:47 (auto-transcript): “Our system is to try to help people, whatever condition they are, to help people. And we cannot help people unless we develop compassion. And to develop compassion, we must be free from selfishness. If we are not free from selfishness, we cannot have compassion. If we don't…”
Contemplation from the Bhagavatam: King Rantideva, near death from thirst, gives his water to an outcaste — and the demigods reveal that they were the guests testing him.

children.topic: Meet a hidden pure devotee today
children.note:
Assume that today a pure devotee in disguise is testing how you treat insignificant people — the irritating co-worker, the slow driver, the rude customer. In the evening, note how your dealings changed. — “These are the daily things that we experience.”

🎙 Maharaj at 84:08 (auto-transcript): “Imagine, today I will conquer. Today I will encounter one hidden pure devotee in disguise as an ordinary person. They are testing how I treat insignificant people. I don't know who it is going to be throughout the day. Treat everyone as if they might be that hidden voice now.…”

Questions from the group and from YouTube.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:02 (auto-transcript): “boat for questions now dear devotees if you have any questions or any reflections or you might raise your hands now I think there was a question yes you do nothing yeah i think was it safe brahmani mataji you had the question from yesterday if it's still relevant you can…”

children.topic: Q5 · Depending on my own efforts?
children.note:
What does it mean to depend on our efforts more than mercy? Maharaj recalls a devotee who said 'I am not the doer' and so did nothing. Endeavour is necessary but never sufficient; many better people than us never got our chance.

🎙 Maharaj at 87:09 (auto-transcript): “do i secretly depend on my efforts austerities or intelligence rather than the mercy of guru and krishna and that question has got me puzzled please would you kindly help me understand this better i i couldn't understand what it means to depend on my efforts austerities or…”

Maharaj: be patient with the mind as a parent is with a child reaching for fire; it makes a huge issue today and calls it useless tomorrow. Hear, practise and pray daily for strength to see its tricks. — “The mind always plays this game with us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 92:10 (auto-transcript): “I just wanted to ask, for example, I have got some service. And somehow, because of my situation, I'm not able to serve with that. So I take help of other devotees who are always there to help me with my services. Then what happens, whenever they make even a single mistake by…”

Seeing a wrong is not an offence — call a spade a spade; a pure devotee is not a stone. Report so that the person can be helped back on track, not crucified; but if we have already judged and tell the senior what to do, it becomes an offence. — “It is not an offense to identify”

🎙 Maharaj at 96:17 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Shila Gurudev. I hope I'm audible. I'm sorry I'm in the car I'm driving, but I just needed to ask first of all, please accept my humble obeisance with Shila Gurudev. uh yesterday about it's about previous classes uh we had you had told us about uh being…”

Eat heavily at midday and lightly at night, sleep before ten thinking of rising early, and the japa is done before 4:30; about six hours of sleep is enough. Design your life around your sadhana. — “it is better for us to plan our japa tomorrow today”

🎙 Maharaj at 100:13 (auto-transcript): “Maharaji, my question is that I have six rounds. I have to study a six rounds before I am going to study a six rounds. foreign foreign foreign foreign Okay, so Prabhu Ji's question is like how should our day be like you know”

children.topic: Q9 · Why is compassion so rare?
children.note:
Compassion comes from selflessness, which purifies the heart until it cannot bear others' suffering. It is a very high quality that must be developed, so few have it. — “it's not something we buy in the market”

🎙 Maharaj at 107:25 (auto-transcript): “one question on YouTube so it's from Anand Prabhuji he says Anand Teshwar Prabhuji Anand Teshwar Prabhuji so he's saying you mentioned about preaching and compassion and that's the mood of our acharyas But we see that at times, devotees can't practice this mode of compassion.…”

nodeData.topic: Session 08 · Compassion Beyond Material Designations
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. From his spiritual master's account of a homeless man struck by a car while his companions stayed seated, Maharaj teaches that character, not words, preaches, and that real compassion comes only from selflessness. Radharani's mercy to a jackal and to a man crying 'Kishori', and Mahaprabhu's mercy to all, show compassion that asks no qualification, while our tendency to value people by wealth, position, tribe or donation exposes a material vision that breeds offences. Questions address interruptions to sadhana, unwelcome advice, searching for pure devotees and building a preaching group. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj takes the devotees back to the 'theatre' for the first session on compassion beyond material designations. Some pain is needed for health: to jump high, you first recoil downward.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:15 (auto-transcript): “If you want to jump, if you want to jump high, what do you do? If you want to jump high, what do you do? We recoil. We recoil to the bottom one. Yes, I have to come down then. You got to spring out. So also, we have to take the little thing to become healthy. So let's go to…”

Maharaj's spiritual master recounts a man running into their car on a preaching trip: he got out to see to him, while the devotees with him stayed in the vehicle, as if the man were disturbing their preaching.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:57 (auto-transcript): “A homeless man incident. This is Shila Prabhupada here. Is Prabhupada? No, Shila Gurudev. It is Sam Sanyansi. Okay. Gurudev, it is Param Gurudev. Param Gurudev has mentioned about his own incident. Yes, he was going for preaching and then. a car locked someone down and the…”

children.topic: If he were a big donor?
children.note:
Had the man been a major temple donor, everyone would have jumped out, offered prasadam and taken him to hospital. So who is the preacher? — “The word is not a preacher.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:04 (auto-transcript): “and the Guru there ask, ask a question. Suppose this man is one of your big donors in the temple. Will we treat him like that? No. Because he is not a big donor, therefore he could be knocked down and passed by to go and preach. But who is preaching? Who is a preacher? The…”

Quoting a thinker, Maharaj says character preaches, not words. Prabhupada convinced people by his character and the compassion in his heart. — “It is the rain that nourishes plants, not thunder.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:00 (auto-transcript): “I just listened to one great thinker. And he said that thunder does not nourish plants. It is the rain that nourishes plants, not thunder. The thunder comes before the rain, is it not? And sometimes they are together. While the rain is falling, the thunder is there. A thunder…”

A pure devotee sees Krishna's energy everywhere, so Prabhupada would close a running tap in the street and told devotees in Mayapur to switch off lights once they could see their palm. Devotees leave lights burning because the mind is covered. — “The mind is blind,”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:55 (auto-transcript): “Because it's spiritual. And pure devotees, so the proper will in the street see a running tap you will go in there to go and close it it's not a spiritual but Prabhupada seeing in everything sees that this is Christian energy being wasted purity is the force and he told…”

Returning from a seminar in Ujjain, Maharaj's driver knocked someone down and wanted to drive on until Maharaj shouted at him to stop. Driving school teaches that you must treat everyone else on the road as a fool — so if you hit one, the fool is you. — “It is you, Mr. Driver, who does not know the rule of driving.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:39 (auto-transcript): “I have the same experience in Calcutta. We're coming from Ujjain. We did a guru seminar in Ujjain. So we were going back to Mayapur. And then the devotee came to take us from the airport to the temple. It was so rough in this time. He was just like if something was shooting…”

Had the man been 'respectable', everyone would have paid attention. Compassion is not only for those in our ashram, our service or our way of thinking; it is a Krishna conscious attitude to all living beings.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:58 (auto-transcript): “True compassion has no boundaries. Later, I was thinking, if this had been a so-called respectable person, every one of us in the car would have been more attentive to this individual. If this were a person in the OT gap, we would have been much more sensitive in some ways.…”

Maharaj asks the group. Devotees answer: feeling another's pain as your own, seeing everyone as brothers and sisters, and taking practical steps to relieve suffering.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:53 (auto-transcript): “So what is compassion? It's a common word which we will. What is compassion? Compassion. Anyone can share with me what is compassion? What do we understand by compassion? This is the word we know, compassion, compassion. anyone cannot say what is compassion it's uh feeling…”

Compassion is being unable to bear others' pain, which only selflessness gives. Charity done to earn heaven is business; a foundation, or even daily book distribution, can be business or show. — “A selfish person cannot be compassionate.”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:04 (auto-transcript): “One cannot be compassionate without being selfless. Only a selfless person can be compassionate. And compassion means what? I cannot tolerate the pain of others. That comes from a person who is selfless. A selfish person cannot be compassionate. We may open an institution for…”

Prabhupada went to the West and patiently trained derelicts into high devotees, building a lasting process to help people — not for money or prestige. — “Just out of love.”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:44 (auto-transcript): “So, the prophet had compassion. That is why he was able to go to the West and tolerate. patiently nurture derelicts derelicts derelicts to train a derelicts and make him a high devotee can be done by only a selfless person who is full of compassion cannot tolerate you see the…”

Prabodhananda Sarasvati calls Radharani an ocean of compassion — an ocean without crocodiles, sharks or timingila fish.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:52 (auto-transcript): “Kabudananda Seleswati describes in Matthew to be ocean of compassion. So when we say ocean of compassion ocean when we look at ocean what are we thinking ocean? Ocean has what? Crocodiles whales sharks timigalas so So, Simatirani is the ocean of mercy. Do we have Timingalas…”

As Maharaj heard it from a senior sannyasi: Radharani heard a jackal crying as boys trapped it in a hole, blocked it with a stone and lit a fire. She sent Lalita and Visakha to free it and brought it to her — and liberated it.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:55 (auto-transcript): “I had from the Solanus Radhana Maharaj. I know I read it, but I had from me. It's a place near Radha Kundu. It's a place near Radha Kundu. When we went there, the place is already like a garbage bin. People dumped in there. But before then, there was a pond there. So Maharaj…”

A wealthy man from Punjab whose wife Kishori had left him roamed Vrindavan crying her name. Lalita said he was no devotee; Radharani answered that he was calling her name, had him brought and delivered him. Chanting 'Radha' daily, says Maharaj, frees one from the cycle of birth. — “Because of chanting Kishori, he got delivered by original Kishori.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:25 (auto-transcript): “So because of his behavior, the wife left him. And due to the attachment he has for his wife, he came to Brundavon and was crying, Kishori, oh, Kishori, oh, my dear Kishori, oh, Kishori, please come back to me. Oh, Kishori, how can I live without you? Please save my life. I…”

People did not come to Caitanya Mahaprabhu for programmes or philosophy; he embraced them and gave the holy name. What qualification did the jackal, or Jagai and Madhai, have?

🎙 Maharaj at 45:07 (auto-transcript): “What is the compassion of Chita Mahaprabhu delivering people? What is the qualification of people who came to Chita Mahaprabhu? They didn't come to him to come and get the Christian program. They didn't come to him to come and hear philosophy. You know, one Sanyasi from…”

Maharaj mimics favouritism: no cleaning service for someone of my tribe and language, all day for another tribe; a phone call when a big donor is sick, none for others. That is material, not compassion. — “These are not compassion.”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:16 (auto-transcript): “Ah, okay, you are in the same country with me. So I will show you compassion. Come, brother, come. oh my dear sister we're the same tribe yeah you speak my language oh come on come on yeah so there's no there's no cleaning service in this temple for you don't do anything oh…”

Reflection: if we want to see Krishna everywhere, we must apply it in every situation. The brahmana with 24 gurus in the Bhagavatam was not unchaste; he was eager to receive Krishna's message from every direction.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:34 (auto-transcript): “Going internal through reflections part one. Who do we really value? Who do we really value? Six minutes. Very good. Who do we really value? If we are seriously trying to see and find Krishna everywhere, trying to glorify Krishna everywhere, and also trying to see how to…”

Claiming that only one's own guru is pure, and pressing others to take initiation from him, brings a Kali-yuga mentality into a Krishna conscious circle. — “dangerous, very dangerous”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:13 (auto-transcript): “No, no, no, you cannot take initiation from somebody said from my guru, only my guru, because Krishna has only one pure devotee in the world. All of you are not pure devotees. If you take initiation from my guru, then when you have difficulty, I'm there to help you. If…”

children.topic: In the car, which one am I?
children.note:
In philosophy we are the one who stepped out; in our dealings we stay inside. Bowing only to a sannyasi's dress is whimsical; a real devotee offers respect to all, because in principle everyone is a devotee. Have I refused help because my schedule seemed more important?

🎙 Maharaj at 50:35 (auto-transcript): “car, who will I have been? The one who stepped out or the one who stayed inside? Be honest and not idealistic. Yes, in philosophy, we are going to say yeah, the one who stepped out. We will say that. I am the one who stepped out. But in dealings, I'm the one who is inside.…”

Devotees share what they wrote, and Maharaj responds.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:54 (auto-transcript): “All right. in my case many times it has happened that someone comes for help and so many times I have turned people away thinking that my devotional schedule is very important this I had shared with you also in one of the sessions in the Katha. So now I was thinking that”

A devotee always turned people away to protect chanting and reading. Maharaj: Krishna is teaching you; once compassion develops, they will come afterwards. Always attend to a real emergency. — “In that case, Krishna wants you to learn something.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:19 (auto-transcript): “many times it has happened that someone comes for help and so many times I have turned people away thinking that my devotional schedule is very important this I had shared with you also in one of the sessions in the Katha. So now I was thinking that does it mean that anytime…”

children.topic: R2 · As my teacher would want
children.note:
A devotee stayed calm under harsh words at home for the first time by thinking how her teacher would want her to behave. Maharaj encourages her to keep doing so.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:59 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, I think, by taking inspiration from the pure devotee i can train myself to get out of the car for example there was one incident actually there are so many incidents but one day there was some tough discussions going on at my home and i got some bad words from one of…”

children.topic: R3 · Devotees in their own world
children.note:
A devotee found neighbours in Mumbai more helpful than temple devotees, and saw a kind brahmacari become withdrawn.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:12 (auto-transcript): “First, I wanted to share that what I felt, Shri LaGurude, that when devotees, they are mostly in their own world. I'm not very old devotee, I'm very neophyte deity. From last seven years or eight years, I'm in devotional service. Before that, people as a human, they were more…”

Maharaj tells of a brahmacari student in Mayapur this year who nursed a sick fellow student; once well, she asked him to marry her. Will he rush to help the next time? Some are hard-hearted, but some became careful through experience — though it should never stop anyone doing the right thing.

🎙 Maharaj at 71:09 (auto-transcript): “Let me ask you one question. This year, in Mayakun, one girl and a boy, they were autistic students together. And after some time, the girl was sick. And because this boy, he knows her from studying together for three months, so he discovered how this girl is sick and nobody…”

A student surrounded by non-devotees all week asks how to keep association. Maharaj: hear lectures and have kirtan at home, chant japa on the way, and go to the temple at weekends. — “that's how you keep yourself balanced”

🎙 Maharaj at 76:48 (auto-transcript): “gurudev my question was that most of the time i devote in my school and coaching for studying and so in there the most of the children that study and sit with me they are not devotees means their thoughts and their habits they are very bad so they've only one day I get to…”

children.topic: R5 · Angry when I can't serve
children.note:
Serving parents instead of devotional duties brings guilt and anger. Maharaj: anger means something is missing — we are not being nourished. When we are, difficulties mean nothing. — “For a devotee who is not advancing, challenges are stumbling blocks.”

🎙 Maharaj at 89:50 (auto-transcript): “it was phrased as a question and this is from shavana mataji kare krishna phila gurudev please accept my humble obeisances gurudev in relation to urmila mataji's question about serving parents or when i have to do other services for me guilt captures that i'm not able to do…”

children.topic: The car matters more than the man
children.note:
The materialist thinks the man who ran into the car was drunk or disturbed and only worries whether the car is damaged. We are conditioned to rank people by wealth, prestige and position, and the mind cannot take us beyond that until spiritual practice lifts us out.

🎙 Maharaj at 78:40 (auto-transcript): “The materialistic mentality, the commercial who formed into us probably has all sorts of mental problems or could have even been drunk. So it may be our tendency to think, well, this is false anyway. He should be careful. Let's see if he's crashed our car. This is the way…”

We look at whether the person spoiled our car, forgetting that a car can be replaced but a person cannot. — “Money can buy the car, but money cannot buy a person,”

🎙 Maharaj at 80:11 (auto-transcript): “We are not going to see what that person is. We're going to see if the person spoil my car. So the car is the most important thing, not the person. Forgetting that we cannot buy a person, but we can buy a car. Money can buy the car, but money cannot buy a person, even though…”

A conditioned soul thinks someone is pure while he holds a post and not after. The pure devotee never thinks himself pure. — “They will treat everyone as pure devotees.”

🎙 Maharaj at 81:08 (auto-transcript): “A conditioned person thinks, now you are a GVC, so you are a pure devotee. If tomorrow you are not a GVC, now you are not a pure devotee. That's a conditioned soul thing. People think some people are important. Some people are unimportant. Yes, one is important only if one is…”

Thinking as we do, Prabhupada would have stayed in Vrindavan enjoying his japa. Because his heart was selfless and compassionate, he went. — “that is why all of us are here today”

🎙 Maharaj at 82:01 (auto-transcript): “If the Prophet was saying that these are rejected conditional conditions, he would have met a devotee. Like what are his govodas? He would have stayed back in India and enjoyed his Christian consciousness. and everything was there all bridges are there and Japa is going very…”

Contemplation: imagine being, in your next life, the homeless, mentally ill man everyone avoids. What would you hope from devotees? Then imagine the person you are today meeting him — would you get out of the car? When you see someone beneath you, think: this could be me in five minutes.

🎙 Maharaj at 84:41 (auto-transcript): “Realization through contemplation, part one. Continue your 30-day notebook with today's focus on equal vision, future, you. Imagine in your next life you are one. A homeless, mentally ill person. Two, the drunk who ran into the car. Three, the person everyone avoids. Let us…”

The Avanti brahmana went from rich merchant to penniless beggar in one life. Our vision is ruled by the mind; with a pure mind we see differently. — “It happened in the same lifetime.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:31 (auto-transcript): “The Avanti Brahmana was a very rich merchant. The next moment, the worst person, completely penniless person, hanging in the street, nothing to eat. It happened in the same lifetime. Not to generally to be the next one because someone changed the situation. But he was so…”

Questions at the end of the session.

🎙 Maharaj at 89:32 (auto-transcript): “So we have some questions. Please keep raising your hands for those who'd like to get questions. uh i will start with one question which we didn't uh cover from the reflection section it was phrased as a question and this is from shavana mataji kare krishna phila gurudev…”

What if relatives resent repeated advice? And should one give money to a drunkard who may spend it on alcohol?

🎙 Maharaj at 92:49 (auto-transcript): “One, the first one but not even with the devotees our close relatives sometimes if you see something is going on and you know that this is going to bring a problem or it's going to put the person in sufferness because of the experience and you you keep talking about it or…”

Once given, money is out of our control, so give prasadam instead. If advice is not accepted, stop and pray to Krishna for the person; pressing on becomes an offence. — “better stop, don't continue”

🎙 Maharaj at 94:44 (auto-transcript): “if we know that If you give money to someone, you cannot control the person. See, this money I'm giving to you, don't drink alcohol with it. We don't have that power. Once you give the money to the person, he's going to do what he likes with it. See, this money, how many?…”

children.topic: Q2 · How to find a pure devotee?
children.note:
Maharaj: we are blind, so searching is a waste. Their qualities are in scripture; follow the process sincerely and Krishna shows from within who is pure. Searching usually means looking for faults. — “I'm just looking for fault”

🎙 Maharaj at 97:20 (auto-transcript): “this is instead of searching you just follow the pure devotee but for us to follow the pure devotee we would need to search for a pure devotee i mean in our case i mean we already have i mean so how should we understand this statement that we should not be using our time…”

children.topic: Q3 · Not wanting to see non-devotees?
children.note:
How does Maharaj's opening joke fit with seeing the soul? He means the face turned away from Krishna: he once asked a scowling man at an airport to smile. Why look at that when we could see Krishna's and Radharani's smiling faces? — “Why are you twisting the face?”

🎙 Maharaj at 99:49 (auto-transcript): “so the next question what there was and I was saying that please forgive me for the next question because I'm not sure if I might be creating an offense was it that right at the start of the lecture you said you don't like looking at the face of non-devotees and here we are…”

children.topic: Q4 · Whom to welcome in a home group?
children.note:
Should a home programme be for like-minded people, and what of a difficult elderly lady or a man in trouble with the police?

🎙 Maharaj at 103:53 (auto-transcript): “I remember when we were having the purpose-driven church seminars. I don't remember the name of the the author of the book the christian author but he said something about that we should kind of have a target audience when we are preaching like that resonates with who we are…”

We cannot pick people in the street; preach to the crowd, train those who come and let them mature into a core. Protect yourself through proper registration if someone is wanted by police, and engage each person at their level — prasadam and simple service for those who cannot take philosophy. — “we have to boil the milk.”

🎙 Maharaj at 106:39 (auto-transcript): “like minded people How do we know? We cannot go to the streets and look at you and select you. OK, you cannot do like that in the streets. We have to preach to everybody. It is from there we get people who are interested. But even among those who show interest to come, still…”

children.topic: Q5 · Seeing greatness only after departure
children.note:
Why do we appreciate great souls only after they leave? Maharaj: when Mahaprabhu glorified Haridasa Thakura after his departure, others were amazed but Rupa and Sanatana were not — they already knew. 'Had I known' is foolishness; the fortunate appreciate what is present.

🎙 Maharaj at 111:52 (auto-transcript): “Dear Guru Maharaj, I wanted to ask this question privately, But I want to ask you maybe to help maybe other people have, other devotees have this doubt. Dear Guru Maharaj, it is said that the goodness of a man does not know until his absence. And this year, there was a…”

maps.title: Radha Sunya · Session 09 · When the Teacher Leaves the Room

nodeData.topic: Session 09 · When the Teacher Leaves the Room
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing compassion beyond designations, Maharaj warns that good intentions are not enough: a devotee who thinks his own service is all-important becomes narrow-minded, while Krishna made society, like the body, a unit in which every part matters. Our consciousness shows in little things — how we treat juniors and peers, and how we behave when the teacher is not watching — and Prabhupada, who met his guru only a few times, proved the true disciple by acting on his words. Questions cover hearing that sticks, offences and surrender, keeping the mood of the holy places, and parents who blaspheme. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Day nine takes compassion a step further. The road to hell is paved with good intentions: a book distributor can be harsh and condescending because he thinks his service matters more than anyone else's.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:51 (auto-transcript): “Taking compassion is a step further. We are trying to understand the danger of apartheid with the mind, with the intention to overcome apartheid. That is the rule. So we are going deeper into compassion. All right? Good intentions are not enough.”

Prabhupada said news of book distribution made him want to live — and also that he wanted to live when he saw palatable prasadam, and told devotees to distribute prasadam profusely. Maharaj jokes: close the kitchen, send everyone on sankirtan, and see how many days it lasts.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:40 (auto-transcript): “So the Papa says, when I hear the book distribution, it gives me love. I'm a liar because when I hear how many books are going out, I have a strong desire to live on. Therefore, if you love Prabhupada, if you are proper to do that, do what? Don't distribution. That is fine.…”

If everyone goes out and the temple, kitchen and altar are left, is that Krishna consciousness? Book distribution, kitchen, cleaning and management must work together, like the parts of a phone. — “That is a team, that's a unit.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:45 (auto-transcript): “Everything in Christian consciousness counts. Everything. Therefore, we should look for balanced life. Balanced life. Both distribution department, kitchen department, data department, cleaning department, managing department, all departments who harmoniously work together.…”

This mentality heads toward Radha-sunya, away from the mercy of the one who oversees bhakti. The narrow, selfish kripana insists everyone think, dress and eat as he does; the mahatma knows how to engage everyone, as Prabhupada did and as Rantideva engaged his whole kingdom. — “A devotee is broad-minded.”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:45 (auto-transcript): “This is narrow-mindedness. A devotee is broad-minded. Sister Papa spoke heavily about Kripanas. Kripanas means what? Narrow-minded. Narrow, selfish person. Doesn't think broadly. A broad-minded person. A broad-minded person, a person includes everyone and everything in this…”

In the spiritual world everyone complements everyone else; there all contradictions are unified in Krishna. That is spirituality.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:12 (auto-transcript): “What do we see in the spiritual world? Everyone is together complementing each other. Everything. There's no ambiguity in the spiritual world. It doesn't exist. All contradictions become unified in Krishna. That is spirituality. That is Krishna consciousness. Yes. It is not a…”

Krishna created the four varnas as one unit. Without sudras, who brings wood for the brahmana's sacrifice? Can a brahmana milk a cow? The vaisya produces food, the ksatriya protects, the brahmana gives knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:41 (auto-transcript): “It is not a mistake that Krishna created the four departments to make a unit. It's not. Four departments to the society. with it. Brahmanas, Sattaya, Baisa, Sudra. So if you remove Sudra from the community, right? Useless. Remove Sudra from the community. How useful would be…”

The hand, calling the stomach lazy, refused to feed it. By afternoon everything was burning and weak, and the hand had no strength left to hold the food — so it fed the stomach and the whole body worked again.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:10 (auto-transcript): “very nice story very nice story to facilitate this the stomach is more represent Vaisya. Hand represent Satriya. The head represent Brahmana. The leg represent Sudra. So the hand protested. We are doing everything. The hand is doing everything. What is it? You're too much.…”

Many powerful book distributors, even Prabhupada's disciples, left the movement through aparadha — insensitivity to other departments. In the spiritual world the residents compete to serve one another. — “It's all competition to serve better.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:16 (auto-transcript): “So if one has a condescending mentality, both distributors, the grace, we have seen so many powerful distributors who have learned this movement, powerful, even proper disciples. Why? Aparada. Due to being insensitive to appreciate other departments. So this mentality is…”

Maharaj reads the definition of bhakti as engaging the senses in the service of their master, and stresses its two fruits: freedom from every designation and purified senses. Sinful reactions are destroyed and love of God develops when we hear about Krishna and serve.

Our consciousness shows less in how we serve before the deities than in the small things we do and say.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:18 (auto-transcript): “The little things reveal everything. The little things reveal everything. It is not always the big thing that draws attention to our state of consciousness as much as the little things we do and say. Powerful. The real quality of our consciousness is not so much based on how…”

children.topic: What's most important in this house?
children.note:
Maharaj asks the group. Answers: Radha-Syamasundara, the guru, Srila Prabhupada, sincere devotees, the books, mahaprasadam, love among devotees, consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:05 (auto-transcript): “piece many times. Let me do it again. In this house, what is the most important thing in this house? This house, what is the most important thing in this house? The altar with the deities, the The Supreme Presence of God is there. Treasury, donors and boxes there. Accountants…”

Without the key you cannot enter to see the deity, hear Prabhupada or use any of the riches inside. It is quality, not quantity. — “Of all the things you mentioned, the smallest is the key.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:07 (auto-transcript): “The most important thing, temple. Oh yeah, a temple. The most important thing in this house is the key. Without the key, you will worship your deity. You enter the house, you worship your deity. You enter the house without the key to worship your deity with all your money.…”

The common mentality treats juniors as servants to exploit, or is kind only to use them. Position, fame and prestige are like decorating a dead body if consciousness is wrong; it is tested every day. — “If the consciousness is not correct,”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:29 (auto-transcript): “How do we treat our genius? My slave. I'm my slave. Like general mentality. General mentality. Who treats the genius? Yeah, object of my exploitation. That's all. Yes. Very rare to find someone who treats genius as special. Even if you see someone treating genius very nicely,…”

children.topic: When the teacher leaves the room
children.note:
It is easy to look devotional in class, before the deities or in the guru's presence. Character shows when the teacher is gone.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:41 (auto-transcript): “When the teacher leaves the room, it is easy to appear very devotional or reverential in the Bhagavatam class. hearing the class with attention in front of the deities having darshan or directly in service to our guru where the physical presence is like us. That reference…”

Prahlada took over his class to teach devotion; we take over to speculate and joke. Jumping into a role before one is qualified is an upstart mentality. — “We become the teacher.”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:17 (auto-transcript): “If you want to know a student, when the teacher is not in the classroom, When the teacher is in the classroom, everybody will be obedient students, because the teacher is there. The moment he saves us, we become our teacher ourselves. We become the teacher. We take over the…”

Those who lived with Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati daily began dividing his property even before he left; he lamented and wished he could sell the marble to print books. Prabhupada took that instruction literally: any money he received, he thought of books. — “if you get money, print books.”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:11 (auto-transcript): “Sr. Papa did not live with the Swiss master for the whole of his life. He didn't. He met the special master occasionally, a few times, but he represented the special master. Those who live with him every day, they die with him every day, they sleep with him every day, they…”

When the guru is not physically present we see who has really heard: that disciple contemplates the teachings quietly and manifests them, empowered. — “That is the time to prove it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:39 (auto-transcript): “heart is different the heart is pure so when the special master is not physically present. That is the time to know who is a bona fide disciple and who has been hearing what the teacher has been teaching all this time. That is the time to prove it. That is the time you know…”

children.topic: Does my sincerity rise or collapse?
children.note:
Reflection: how does my behaviour change when authorities aren't watching, or with peers rather than in formal settings? Do I serve to be seen, or because I am devoted?

🎙 Maharaj at 53:27 (auto-transcript): “true reflection. The realities of character, we have five minutes for that. However, there may be one student in the group who will be even more conscious, conscientious, because the teacher is not there. It is a personal reflection. Take a good look at your personal life.…”

Devotees share their reflections and Maharaj responds.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:07 (auto-transcript): “Shweta Mataji has raised her hand yes Mataji can you unmute my respectful and humble obeisance is on to you the answer of all four points is I fall down and I mean not with that sincerity I do and I fail I don't know I should use fail word or not but I feel I am fallen”

children.topic: R1 · Clean only when Guru visits?
children.note:
A devotee rose at 1 a.m. to clean the stairs while Maharaj was in Lagos, but not otherwise. Maharaj: clean regularly, as if he is always coming; prepare every day, not only before a visit. — “Yes, you should clean.”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:55 (auto-transcript): “Shilagurudev, it is, like, what I felt that when you were there, what we were doing, and when you were not there, there is a practical difference is there. So that I wanted to understand. It should be like that or it should not be like that. Yes, it's really like that. You…”

children.topic: R2 · Enthusiasm fades after he leaves
children.note:
Sadhana was easy while Maharaj was in Brazil and hard after. Maharaj: keep what you heard in mind and see him wherever you are, and the experience stays. Keep the fire burning. — “that after we hear, we don't hear.”

🎙 Maharaj at 67:04 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, good neighbor. Please accept in my home obeisances. So I have a comment and a question about that also. My experience is when the Guru is present, for example, now he was with us in Brazil, sadhana, enthusiastic everything goes very easily no need to put so much…”

children.topic: R3 · Devotees who perform for leaders
children.note:
A devotee is discouraged by devotees who behave well only before the guru and leaders. Maharaj: everything is an offering for our own benefit; behaving differently when unseen is duplicity and brings aparadha. Such people are like the cadaver a medical student needs. — “That is character building.”

🎙 Maharaj at 75:13 (auto-transcript): “better. Yes, if a devotee wants to make an advancement, he should always remember that everything we do is our offerings to Krishna, to Sushama, everything we do. Therefore, as you do everything nicely, because it is me who is benefiting, not somebody else. So if I'm going to…”

Who is right does not matter; who does the right thing does. If one devotee strikes and the other strikes back to 'teach a lesson', both are wrong; the right one accepts without retaliating. — “Both of us have done the wrong thing.”

🎙 Maharaj at 77:58 (auto-transcript): “We already discussed that who is right and who is wrong is not important. Who does the right thing is important. No, no, no, no, Guruji, you know, Govind Bhuja, she gave me a blow on my face. And she did first, you know, Guruji, I was very gentle, very nice, devoted,…”

Maharaj's guru once seated each devotee while the others listed his faults. Afterwards he asked Maharaj why he was angry; Maharaj said he had not retaliated, and his guru replied that he had still not passed fully. — “You didn't pass 100%.”

🎙 Maharaj at 80:56 (auto-transcript): “when we finished the exercise and when we declared everything finished there was massaging guru and he said why are you angry I didn't say anything again because I know he has gotten everything why are you angry? so you think I don't know? why are you angry? I'm sorry I'm…”

A good student asks what the teacher wants and, when the teacher is absent, becomes even more careful, reflecting on what was said and the message behind it. Maharaj adds: don't become Mr. Right.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:49 (auto-transcript): “Go internal through reflection. The real, the good student mentality. A good student thinks, what does my teacher want me to do? When the teacher is not present, to be directly asked questions or to monitor the students. The good student is even more meticulous and careful,…”

Notebook exercise: divide a page into three columns and track speech, presence, cleanliness, eating and phone use in formal and casual settings — for example japa in the temple and alone at home. Maharaj objects to devotees saying 'devour' about food; we honour prasadam.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:34 (auto-transcript): “Realization through contemplation. This is very powerful. Continue your 30-day notebook with today's focus on equal vision. Divide the page into three columns. One, formal setting. Two, casual setting. Three, the gap. Now, track these little things throughout your day. How…”

Devotees abroad asked whether Maharaj sees the food they offer him. If we doubt it, the offering is a mere ritual; with real conviction that we deal with a person, it becomes prasadam. — “if they are different, that means cheating”

🎙 Maharaj at 90:01 (auto-transcript): “sometime back some devotees they send a message Guru, when we offer prasadam to you in my country, do you see do you see you ain't good tell me you're in Nigeria and Mauritius I'm offering food in Mauritius you see you eat it I said what do you think yes no this is what do…”

Chanting to show off is like the parrot that repeats perfectly but never practises, or the bhurunda bird of the Himalayas that repeats the sages' scriptures exactly and practises nothing.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:51 (auto-transcript): “I was chanting to show off to others. Yes. That is parod. Parod repeats everything as they heard it. Perfectly. Everything. But parod does not practice. it has ability to repeat but no practice also there's another bird which is called burunda burunda bird burunda bird lives…”

Questions from the group and the chat.

🎙 Maharaj at 98:11 (auto-transcript): “We have a question from Shivani Mataji. Shall we take Gurudev? Yes. Shivani Mataji? She's retired since. I mean, obviously, so she will be retired. So let's take her question. She can bring her hand up. Okay. And do that. Hi, Krishna Mahesh. please except for most humble of…”

A devotee is happy while hearing and sinks when she cannot hear all day. Maharaj: Prabhupada did not sit with his guru daily; real hearing means practising what we hear — reflect on it, take notes and review them so it enters the heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 98:43 (auto-transcript): “first is life is miserable and I'm struggling a lot somehow but whenever I am acting according to the instructions or maybe I'm hearing somehow to my teachers or the devotees that moment of the day is the most blissful for me at that time I'm able to act like a devotee but as…”

Asked later how to hear lectures from the heart, Maharaj says it is like eating when hungry: know why you hear. A drowning man grabs the rope without asking for proof; Brahma tells Narada that Maya cannot touch him because he holds on with great zeal.

🎙 Maharaj at 115:45 (auto-transcript): “Next one? Yes, Gurudev. Next one is from Vishnumurthi Sevak Prabhuji. He's asking, how do we cultivate our heart? Like, how do we hear lectures from our heart? How do we cultivate that feeling from hearing lecture effectively? the question is like how do i eat when i'm hungry…”

If every soul eventually becomes a devotee, how does an offence to a future devotee count? Maharaj: we pay for everything; no conditioned soul lives without sin. Krishna's call to surrender in the Gita is compulsory — we surrender willingly now or are forced at death. — “The only security for anyone in this world is to become a devotee.”

🎙 Maharaj at 103:09 (auto-transcript): “he is asking Hare Krishna Gurudev please accept my humble obeisances to your lotus feet If could be possible, I have a question from previous session that I couldn't ask. In the story of Dhruva Maharaj, we see how Suruji offended him and how Dhruva Maharaj in time became a…”

children.topic: Q3 · Keeping the mood of the dhama
children.note:
Consciousness rises in the holy place and fades at home. Maharaj recalls cleaning at Radha Kunda thinking of Radharani's mercy and keeping such memories alive; repeat what you want to remember. Don't praise a blind man so much that he throws away his stick. — “We use the word, keep the fire burning.”

🎙 Maharaj at 108:07 (auto-transcript): “if you don't hear properly you don't hear properly you don't keep note you don't refer to them you don't remember I was in the dam we visited Radha Khun we did cleaning we did cleaning I was cleaning I was picking these things I was speaking, I was brushing I was cleaning so…”

Good intentions lead toward right consciousness, but you can still make serious mistakes — like asking a doctor to end a suffering father's life. Have good intentions and build on them. — “So our good intention is not sufficient.”

🎙 Maharaj at 111:08 (auto-transcript): “next we have krishna mohini gaurangi mataji mataji can you unmute please thank you so much for the wonderful class my question was it was mentioned that how maintaining a good consciousness is very important at the same time we heard that good intentions are not always enough…”

children.topic: Q5 · Parents who criticise the guru
children.note:
Those who blaspheme your guru and the movement are not favourable; to save yourself, keep distance. Accept what is favourable even if you dislike it, and reject what is unfavourable. — “Things which are not favorable should be rejected.”

🎙 Maharaj at 113:09 (auto-transcript): “One is from Krishna Premi Indulekha Mataji. She's asking, Hare Krishna, dear Gurudev, if parents at home criticize our Guru and Vaishnavas who are serving sincerely, it is difficult to behave like them, like we would behave in Goloka. It really spoils my consciousness leading…”
